newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia's Unibanka to consider merger with Zemes.
newsitem.headline: Latvia's Unibanka to consider merger with Zemes.

text.p: The shareholders of leading Latvian bank Unibanka on Thursday gave their backing to the bank's board to investigate merging with the Baltic country's seventh largest bank, Zemes Bank.
Unibank is part-owned by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Swedfund and is the leading share quoted on the stock exchange.
An Unibanka spokeswoman said the bank's directors would now gather all the necessary documents and information and make a final decision on whether to merge with Zemes Bank.
The final decision will be taken at another shareholders' meeting in either February or March, the spokeswoman added.
The EBRD also has a stake in Zemes Bank, which had capital at the end of October of 7.36 million lats while Unibanka's was 25.85 million lats.
Unibanka's assets at the end of October were 142.58 million lats and Zemes Bank's 45.74 million lats.
A merger would be the first between the top 10 banks in Latvia, which was hit in the middle of last year by a banking crisis.
The country has been gradually recovering from the crisis but analysts expect there to be more mergers among the more than 30 banks which operate in a country of just 2.5 million people.
